Hi Samir - great speaking with you and Tom yesterday. Looping Rishi (solutions) and Neha (security ops) so we can get the questionnaire and follow-ups completed. Below are answers to the items you raised and next steps.

SOC 2: We completed SOC 2 Type II in November 2026. I attached the SOC2_Report_2026_v1.pdf for your team's review. If you need an SOC2 bridge letter or redacted report, we can provide that under NDA.

GDPR / HIPAA / BAA: Redwood supports GDPR requirements and can sign a BAA for customers handling PHI. For HIPAA-bound workloads we recommend our Dedicated or Private deployment options (VPC/on-prem) - we have standard BAA language and can share a template.

Data deletion SLA (overview):
- Active data: deletion requests through the API/console trigger an asynchronous workflow - typical removal from active storage within 24-72 hours.
- Backups: snapshot backups are retained by default for 90 days. Deletion from backups is governed by our backup lifecycle; by default data will be removed from backups on the next retention cycle (within 90 days). We can contractually tighten that for Enterprise/Dedicated customers (example: 30-day backup deletion SLA) as part of a negotiated agreement.
- Logs / audit logs: default retention is 30 days for request/trace logs. We can configure shorter retention windows (e.g., 7/14 days) for EU-only data subject to deployment model and configuration.

Encryption & keys: all customer data (active storage, logs, backups) is encrypted at rest. We support customer-managed KMS keys for Dedicated/Private customers and default service-managed keys for Hosted.

Hi Lydia - quick answers below, and happy to jump on a call to walk through details with Neha.

1) Backups & deletion propagation: deletion requests remove data from active stores within 24-72 hours. Backups are snapshot-based and not immediately rewritten on delete; deleted items are removed on the next backup lifecycle. Default backup retention is 90 days, which means recovery windows may still include deleted items until the snapshot containing them expires. For Enterprise / Dedicated customers we can negotiate a backup-deletion SLA (example: 30-day maximum window) and/or implement targeted snapshot purge procedures under contract.

2) Immutability: backups are not WORM by default. We maintain immutable logs for forensic/audit purposes where required, but standard snapshot backups are lifecycle-managed and can be purged per contractual terms. If Amaya requires WORM/immutable backups for regulatory reasons we can discuss specialized retention and access controls (usually part of Dedicated/Private offerings).

3) Log retention: the 30-day default is configurable. For Hosted customers we offer configuration down to 14 days for log retention; for EU-only 7-day retention we typically recommend Dedicated or Private so logs can be segmented and retention enforced at the tenant level. We'll document the exact configuration options in the questionnaire.

Encryption & keys: reiterating - active data, backups, and logs are encrypted at rest. We offer customer-managed keys (KMS) for Dedicated/Private and service-managed keys for Hosted. Key rotation and access controls are documented in the SOC2 and vendor questionnaire.
